current.text: He signed with Brooklyn for 2 years and 18 million as veteran depth. The deal includes a mutual option.
He is projected as Brooklyn's sixth man, in a bench rotation with Noah Clowney, Mo Wagner, Danny Wolf and Nolan Traore.
He can give capable minutes if Brooklyn asks him to start.
He needs about 27 minutes a game to matter in 12-team category leagues. Treat him as a stash or a late flyer, not a must-roster player, and do not target him aggressively.
Brooklyn is projected to be one of the worst teams. Slater predicts about 28 wins.

Houston controls Brooklyn's pick, so the Nets have no reason to tank. They are also running a development season, so second-half minutes could shift to young players like Minott, Clowney, Brown and Demin. That makes March minutes uncertain for veteran depth.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied with Boston for the most in the league. With a March 28 end, its playoff schedule is 3-4-3 (10 games) with only one back-to-back in the playoff weeks.

durable.text: He is a low-usage wing. He brings few turnovers and solid steals, but low points, rebounds and assists.
